  expected=$("$HORIZON_GIT" rev-parse refs/heads/main)

  GIT_INDEX_FILE="$index_path" "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree "$expected"
  GIT_INDEX_FILE="$index_path" "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- "$item_path" "$history_path" "$comment_path"

  rm "$index_path"
  if "$HORIZON_GIT" update-ref refs/heads/main "$commit" "$expected"; then
    printf "committed=%s'"\\nparent=%s\\n\" \""'$commit" "$expected"
    "$HORIZON_GIT" show --stat --oneline --no-renames "$commit"
    exit 0
  fi
  attempt=$((attempt + 1))
done
printf "CAS_RETRIES_EXHAUSTED'"\\n\" >&2
exit 1"

     2	
     3	Adopted after the 2026-07-16 evening wave's four incidents (I-0149). These rules extend the
     4	standing handoff protocol (07-14/14b/15) for any session running two or more lanes in this
     5	workspace.
     6	
     7	## 1. Ledger commits: private index + compare-and-swap (the shared-index race)
     8	
     9	All lanes commit through one `workspace.git`; concurrent `git add`+`commit` through the
    10	SHARED index can interleave and record spurious deletions of another lane's
    11	freshly-committed files (happened in `6197c9676`, 862 lines vanished from HEAD, restored
    12	byte-identical in `a640fef5b`). Concurrent lanes MUST commit via a private index:
    13	
    14	```bash
    15	cd /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
    16	GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git
    17	export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
    18	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. read-tree HEAD
    19	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. add <ONLY your paths…>
    20	TREE=$(git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. write-tree)
    21	PARENT=$(git --git-dir=$GD rev-parse HEAD)
    22	COMMIT=$(git --git-dir=$GD -c user.name="Archon Horizon" -c user.email="archon-horizon@local" \
    23	  commit-tree $TREE -p $PARENT -m "<math-first message>
    24	
    25	Archon-Commit: agent
    26	Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>")
    27	git --git-dir=$GD update-ref refs/heads/main $COMMIT $PARENT   # CAS: fails if HEAD moved
    28	unset GIT_INDEX_FILE
    29	```
    30	
    31	If the `update-ref` CAS fails (HEAD moved), re-read HEAD and repeat — never force.
    32	ALWAYS verify afterward: `git --git-dir=$GD show --stat HEAD` must touch only your paths.
    33	A single-lane session may keep the plain `add`+`commit` recipe, but must still verify.
    34	
    35	### 1a. THE RECIPE ABOVE HAS A RACE — read HEAD ONCE, not twice (2026-07-28, run 0072)
    36	
    37	**As written, the recipe reads `HEAD` twice**: once in `read-tree HEAD`, and again several lines
    38	later in `PARENT=$(… rev-parse HEAD)`. If another lane's CAS lands **between those two reads**,
    39	your tree is built from the *old* snapshot while your parent is the *new* commit — and
    40	`update-ref` **succeeds**, because it only checks that the ref has not moved since `rev-parse`.
    41	It never checks that the tree was built from that ref. You publish a stale tree, silently
    42	reverting everything that landed in the window.
    43	
    44	**Measured once, and the measurement is narrow — do not over-read it.** `e964967e8` has parent
    45	`a1ef4d59c` and, diffed against *that parent*, deletes 95 lines of
    46	`informal/w4-rep-critical-path.md`, 52 of `informal/w5-t4-worksheet.md` and 19 of
    47	`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean` — exactly the restore `a1ef4d59c` had just performed, undone.
    48	Its `read-tree` ran before `a1ef4d59c` landed; its parent was captured after. It staged explicit
    49	paths and the pathspec *was* honoured: **the sweep came from the TREE BASE, not the pathspec**,
    50	which is why "stage explicit files" is not a defence and why the symptom is indistinguishable
    51	from §1b's shared-index staleness.
    52	
    53	**Two other lanes audited their own CAS commits the same day (fifteen commits between them,
    54	recipe verbatim) and found zero reverts.** That is consistent with this: the race only fires when
    55	another lane's CAS lands inside your particular window, so clean commits are the expected
    56	outcome, not evidence of absence. The discriminating question is not "did my commits look clean"
    57	but "was my `read-tree` separated from my `rev-parse` by somebody else's commit". Treat §1a as
    58	cheap insurance, not as a diagnosis of every mystery revert — and check §1b too.
    59	
    60	**The fix is one line — capture the parent BEFORE the tree, and read-tree that sha:**
    61	
    62	```bash
    63	PARENT=$(git --git-dir=$GD rev-parse HEAD)     # ONCE, up front
    64	export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
    65	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. read-tree $PARENT      # not "HEAD"
    66	git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. add <ONLY your paths…>
    67	TREE=$(git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. write-tree)
    68	COMMIT=$(git --git-dir=$GD … commit-tree $TREE -p $PARENT -m "…")
    69	git --git-dir=$GD update-ref refs/heads/main $COMMIT $PARENT   # now genuinely atomic
    70	```
    71	
    72	Then a mid-recipe CAS by another lane makes `update-ref` **fail**, you re-read and retry, and the
    73	protocol behaves as it was meant to. The verification step ("must touch only your paths") is what
    74	catches it after the fact — run it every time, and read the file list, not just the count.
    75

    77

-  apply J.superset_covering _ (imageSieve_mem J f s.down)
-  intro V i hi
-  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := hi
-  refine ⟨ULift.up t, ?_⟩
-  apply ULift.ext
-  exact ht

    AlgebraicGeometry.admissibleAbelEtaleSourceIso,
    AlgebraicGeometry.admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap}
  \uses{def:admissibleDivisorRepresentation, def:admissibleAbelMap}
  \leanok
  After raising values to the universe required by the big site and sheafifying, the
  source is identified by subcanonicity with the actual big-etale Yoneda sheaf of
  \(D_{\mathrm{adm}}\). The resulting morphism has target the big-etale sheafification of
  the Sigma Picard presheaf. Identifying that target with the original Picard functor is a
  separate step.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The Sigma Picard functor is a big-etale sheaf]
  \label{thm:pic0SigmaFunctor_isEtaleSheaf}
  \uses{def:pic0SigmaFunctor, thm:pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf,
    def:admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap}
  \notready
  The Sigma-extension of \(\mathrm{pic}^0\) satisfies descent for the big-etale topology,
  and its universe-raised sheaf is canonically isomorphic to the sheafification in
  Definition~\ref{def:admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Etale-local surjectivity of the admissible Abel map]
  \label{thm:admissibleAbel_etaleLocallySurjective}
  \uses{def:admissibleAbelMap, def:admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap}
  \notready
  The concrete admissible Abel transformation is locally surjective for the big-etale
  topology. Equivalently, every degree-zero Picard class lifts to an admissible divisor
  family after an etale cover of the test scheme.
  \source{kleiman-picard}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The sheafified Abel map is the coequalizer of its kernel pair]
  \label{thm:admissibleAbel_etaleCoequalizer}
  \uses{def:admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap,
    thm:admissibleAbel_etaleLocallySurjective}
  \notready
  Local surjectivity makes the sheafified Abel map a regular epimorphism in the category of
  type-valued big-etale sheaves. Hence it is the coequalizer of its pullback kernel pair.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The concrete Abel kernel pair is representable]
  \label{thm:admissibleAbelKernelPair_representable}
  \uses{thm:admissibleAbel_kernel, thm:admissibleDivisorSource_projectLocal}
  \notready
  Construct a scheme \(R\) representing the concrete kernel relation on
  \(D_{\mathrm{adm}}\), identify it with the fibre product over the Picard sheaf, and prove
  that the first projection \(R \to D_{\mathrm{adm}}\) is smooth and proper.
  \source{kleiman-picard}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The Altman--Kleiman effective quotient]
  \label{thm:admissibleAbel_effectiveQuotient}
  \uses{thm:admissibleDivisorSource_projectLocal,
    thm:admissibleAbelKernelPair_representable}
  \notready
  Apply the flat-proper equivalence-relation theorem to construct a scheme
  \(Q = D_{\mathrm{adm}}/R\) over \(\Spec k\), with quotient map
  \(D_{\mathrm{adm}} \to Q\), and identify \(R\) with
  \(D_{\mathrm{adm}} \times_Q D_{\mathrm{adm}}\). This is a construction of the concrete
  quotient, not a theorem with quotient data as a hypothesis.
  \source{kleiman-picard}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Yoneda identification of the quotient]
  \label{thm:admissibleAbel_quotientYoneda}
  \uses{thm:pic0SigmaFunctor_isEtaleSheaf,
    thm:admissibleAbel_etaleCoequalizer,
    thm:admissibleAbel_effectiveQuotient,
    thm:admissibleAbel_kernel}
  \notready
  The Yoneda sheaf of \(Q\) and the degree-zero Picard Sigma functor are coequalizers of
  the same represented kernel pair. The induced isomorphism is compatible with the
  structure maps to \(\Spec k\), and therefore descends from the Sigma-extension to
  \(\mathrm{pic}^0_{\mathrm{Set}}(C)\) on the slice.
  \source{kleiman-picard}
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[The admissible Abel quotient representer]
  \label{def:pic0AdmissibleAbelQuotientRepresenter}
  \uses{thm:admissibleAbel_quotientYoneda, thm:representableBy_overSlice}
  \notready
  The direct endpoint is
  \[
    \operatorname{pic0AdmissibleAbelQuotientRepresenter}(C)
      : \sum_{Q : \Over(\Spec k)}
          \mathrm{RepresentableBy}\bigl(\mathrm{pic0TypeFunctor}(C),Q\bigr).
  \]
  Its body chooses the admissible datum internally, directly consumes
  \(\operatorname{divFunctorAff\_admissible\_representableBy}\), constructs the effective
  quotient above, and returns its Yoneda comparison. It has no representability,
  local-surjectivity, kernel-pair, rational-point, or quotient-data binder.
\end{definition}

    [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]

    (l θ : Y.CechPic) (hθ : 1 ≤ classDeg K θ) :
    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀, ∀ D : Y.CurveDivisor,
      CurveDivisor.picClass K D = l * θ ^ n →
      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K D) 1) := by
  obtain ⟨D₀, hD₀⟩ := CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq K l
  obtain ⟨m₀, hm₀⟩ := subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1 π hπ D₀
  set F : Y.CurveDivisor := fiberWeilDivisor π with hF
  set d' : ℤ := CurveDivisor.deg K F with hd'
  have hd'pos : 0 < d' := by rw [hd', hF]; exact zero_lt_deg_fiberWeilDivisor π
  set φ : Y.CechPic := CurveDivisor.picClass K F with hφ
  have hφdeg : classDeg K φ = d' := by rw [hφ, hd', classDeg_picClass]
  set gtld : ℤ := 1 - Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) with hgtld
  refine ⟨(m₀ * d' + gtld).toNat, fun n hn D hD => ?_⟩
  -- the residual class and its degree
  set c : Y.CechPic := θ ^ n * (φ ^ m₀)⁻¹ with hc
  have hcdeg : classDeg K c = n * classDeg K θ - m₀ * d' := by
    rw [hc, classDeg_mul, classDeg_inv, classDeg_pow, classDeg_pow, hφdeg]; ring
  have hlarge : gtld ≤ classDeg K c := by
    rw [hcdeg]
    have h1 : (m₀ * d' + gtld : ℤ) ≤ (n : ℤ) :=
      le_trans (Int.self_le_toNat _) (by exact_mod_cast hn)
    have h2 : (n : ℤ) ≤ (n : ℤ) * classDeg K θ :=
      le_mul_of_one_le_right (Int.natCast_nonneg n) hθ
    linarith
  -- an effective witness of the residual class
  obtain ⟨W, hWc⟩ := CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq K c
  have hWdeg : 1 ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K W + Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) := by
    have hWc' : classDeg K c = CurveDivisor.deg K W := by rw [← hWc, classDeg_picClass]

    rw [hF]; exact hm₀ m₀ le_rfl
  have hpeel : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (D₀ + m₀ • F + E)) 1) :=
    peel_effective (D₀ + m₀ • F) E hEnonneg hbase
  exact subsingleton_hModule_one_of_picClass_eq K (hD'class.trans hD.symm) hpeel

theorem h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one
    [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
    [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
    (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (hsub : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K D) 1)) :
    (Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K D) : ℤ)

  have h1 : Sheaf.chi (Y.divisorSheaf K D) = (Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K D) : ℤ) :=
    Sheaf.chi_eq_h0 hsub
  have h2 := chi_divisorSheaf K D
  rw [h1] at h2
  omega

# B-5 step 3: the vanishing threshold at the splitting field is UNIFORM, and it is π-free

## Current endpoint (2026-07-30)

The earlier analysis below correctly proves that a legal index calibrated at a threshold `b`
has chart parameter `n = b`, but it silently specialised `b` to the *smallest named bound*
`B = M·δ + g`.  Vanishing is monotone: any `n ≥ B` is equally valid.  The declarations
`admissibleCoverageParameter` through `exists_uniform_admissibleCoverageChart_eq_univ` choose
`n = B·d₁`, prove it is both above `B` and a divisor degree, produce one legal chart index, and
show that its chart locus is `Set.univ` for every `pic⁰` class.  Thus the former residue
`IsDivisorDegree C g` is not an obligation of coverage; it belongs only to the fixed-`B` branch
retained later in this file and in `Pic0ChartIndexLedgerFeed`.

`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` settles that at a chart index legal at parameter
`n` the coverage hypothesis `hb` of `mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` forces `b = n`, and
that `b = g` is false in general (`hb_forces_h0_eq_one`).  Its item 3 then names the residue:
*reconcile the chart parameter with the threshold*.  Both that file and
`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean`'s retraction treat the threshold `b` — DAT-0a's bound
**at the splitting field `L`** — as a per-`L` quantity that has to be obtained before the
reconciliation can even be stated.

**That is where the pricing is wrong, and this file measures why.**  Two separate points:

* **RETRACTED, 2026-07-30, by a fresh-context audit and reproduced by the author (inbox
  `I-1349`/`I-1350`).**  This bullet read: *"DAT-0a itself is not instantiable at `L` ... there
  is no `relCurve C L ⟶ P1 L` anywhere in this tree, so a lane trying to instantiate DAT-0a at
  a splitting field is trying to build a morphism the project does not have."*  **That is
  false.**  `exists_isFinite_isDominant_toP1` (`Curve/MapToP1.lean:126`) *produces* such a
  morphism for any bundle satisfying the curve hypotheses, and
  `Curve/BaseChangeInstances.lean` supplies those for `baseChangeBundle C L`
  (`instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionSndLeft`, `instIsProperSndLeft`,
  `instGeometricallyIrreducibleSndLeft`).  So DAT-0a *is* instantiable at a splitting field,
  in three `haveI`s.  The error was grepping for the arrow as a *term* when the answer was an
  `exists_`-producer quantified over curves — a producer census, not a term census, is what
  settles "no such morphism exists".
* **The threshold does not need DAT-0a.**  `subsingleton_hModule_one_of_witness`
  (`RiemannRoch/WindowFieldTransport.lean:87`) is the **π-free peeling**: a *single* witness
  divisor with vanishing `H¹` gives vanishing for every divisor of degree
  `≥ deg W₀ + 1 − χ`.  And `windowN C L hπ g` (`:307`) is such a witness on `relCurve C L`
  for every field extension `L/k`, with `subsingleton_h1_windowN` and
  `deg_windowN = M·δ`.

## THE HEADLINE IS A RE-DERIVATION — read this before citing `subsingleton_h1_of_ledger_bound`

**Also from the 2026-07-30 audit (`I-1349`), and it is the more important correction.**
`subsingleton_h1_of_windowA_le_deg` (`Picard/DivSchemeSeedUnivFibre.lean:259`, landed

/-- Equality of widened Abel values is equality of their relative Picard classes on every
affine open of the test scheme. -/
theorem abelDivAff'_eq_iff_forall_relPicMk_picClass_eq
    [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (s₁ s₂ : divFamZarAff C n T) :
    abelDivAff' C n T s₁ = abelDivAff' C n T s₂
      ↔ ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,

underlying divisor families, affine-locally on the test scheme. -/
theorem chartValueAff_eq_iff_forall_relPicMk_picClass_eq

    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (s₁ s₂ : divFamZarAff C n T) :
    chartValueAff C n m Z T s₁ = chartValueAff C n m Z T s₂
      ↔ ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,

            = relPicMk C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)) (s₂.1 U).picClass :=
  (chartValueAff_eq_iff_abelDivAff'_eq C n m Z T s₁ s₂).trans

  1270	Picard functors, and each one is more likely to be representable than
  1271	the preceding.  In this section, they all are formally introduced and
  1272	compared.
  1273	
  1274	\begin{dfn}\label{df:aPf}
  1275	 The {\it absolute Picard functor} $\Pic_X$ is the functor from  the
  1276	 category of (locally Noetherian) $S$-schemes $T$ to the category of
  1277	abelian groups defined by the formula
  1278		$$\Pic_X(T):=\Pic(X_T).$$
  1279	\end{dfn}
  1280	
  1281	The absolute Picard functor  is a ``prepared presheaf'' in this
  1282	sense: given any family of  $S$-schemes $T_i$, we have
  1283		$$\Pic_X\bigl(\textstyle\coprod T_i\bigr)=\prod\Pic_X(T_i).$$
  1284	 Hence, given a covering family $\{T_i\to T\}$ in the Zariski topology,
  1285	the \'etale topology, or any other Grothendieck topology on the category
  1286	of $S$-schemes, there is no harm, when we consider the sheaf associated
  1287	to $\Pic_X$, in working simply with the single map $T'\to T$ where
  1288	$T':=\coprod T_i$.  And doing so lightens the notation, making for
  1289	easier reading. Therefore, we do so throughout, calling $T'\to T$ simply
  1290	a {\it covering\/} in the given topology.
  1291	
  1292	The absolute Picard functor $\Pic_X$ is never a separated presheaf in
  1293	the Zariski topology.  Indeed, take an $S$-scheme $T$ that carries an
  1294	invertible sheaf $\mc N$ such that $f^*_T\mc N$ is nontrivial.  (For
  1295	example, take $T:=\I P^1_X$ and $\mc N:=\mc O_{\!T}(1)$.  Then the diagonal
  1296	map $X\to X\x X$ induces a section $g$ of $f_T$; that is, $gf_T=1_T$.
  1297	Hence $f^*_T\mc N$ is nontrivial.)  Now, there exists a Zariski covering
  1298	$T'\to T$ such that the pullback $\mc N|T'$ is trivial; here, $T'$ is
  1299	simply the disjoint union of the subsets in a suitable ordinary open
  1300	covering of $T$.  So the pullback $f^*_{T'}\mc N|X_{T'}$ is trivial too.
  1301	Thus $\Pic_X(T)$ has a nonzero element whose restriction is zero in
  1302	$\Pic_X(T')$.
  1303	
  1304	According to descent theory, every representable functor is a sheaf in
  1305	the Zariski topology \emdash in fact, in the \'etale and fppf
  1306	topologies as well.  Therefore, the absolute Picard functor $\Pic_X$ is never
  1307	representable.  So, in the hope of obtaining a representable functor
  1308	that differs as little as possible from $\Pic_X$, we now define a
  1309	sequence of three successively more promising relative functors.
  1310	
  1311	\begin{dfn}\label{df:Pfs}
  1312	  The {\it relative Picard functor} $\Pic_{X/S}$ is defined by
  1313		$$\Pic_{X/S}(T):=\Pic(X_T)\big/\Pic(T).$$
  1314	 Denote its associated sheaves in the Zariski, \'etale, and fppf
  1315	topologies  by
  1316		$$\Pic_{(X/S)\zar},\ \Pic_{(X/S)\et},\
  1317		\Pic_{(X/S)\fppf}.$$
  1318	 \end{dfn}
  1319	
  1320	We now have a sequence of five Picard functors, and each one maps
  1321	naturally into the next.  So each one maps naturally into any of its
  1322	successors.  If the latter functor is one of the three just displayed,
  1323	then it is a sheaf in the indicated topology; in fact, it is the sheaf
  1324	associated to any one of its predecessors, and the map between them is
  1325	the natural map from a presheaf to its associated sheaf, as is easy to
  1326	check.  In particular, the three displayed sheaves are the sheaves
  1327	associated to the absolute Picard functor $\Pic_X$, as well as to the
  1328	relative Picard functor $\Pic_{X/S}$.
  1329	
  1330	Since $\Pic_{X/S}$ is not a priori a sheaf, it is remarkable that it is
  1331	representable so often in practice.
  1332	
  1333	Note that, for every $S$-scheme $T$, each $T$-point of
  1334	$\Pic_{(X/S)\fppf}$, or element of $\Pic_{(X/S)\fpqc}(T)$, is
  1335	represented by an invertible sheaf $\mc L'$ on $X_{T'}$ for some
  1336	fppf-covering $T'\to T$.    Moreover, there must
  1337	be an fppf-covering $T''\to T'\x_T T'$ such that the two pullbacks of
  1338	$\mc L'$ to $X_{T''}$ are isomorphic \emdash or to put it informally, the
  1339	restrictions of $\mc L'$ must agree on a covering of the overlaps.
  1340	
  1341	Furthermore, a second such sheaf $\mc L_1$ on $X_{T_1}$ represents the
  1342	same $T$-point if and only if there is an fppf-covering $T_1'\to T_1\x_T
  1343	T'$ such that the pullbacks of $\mc L'$ and $\mc L_1$ to $X_{T_1'}$ are
  1344	isomorphic.  Technically, this condition includes the preceding one,
  1345	which concerns the case where $T_1=T'$ and $\mc L_1=\mc L'$ since $\mc
  1346	L'$ must represent the same $T$-point as itself.  Of course, similar
  1347	considerations apply to the Picard functors for the Zariski and \'etale
  1348	topologies as well.
  1349	
  1350	\begin{ex}\label{ex:Alr}
  1351	 Given an $S$-scheme $T$ of the form $T=\Spec(A)$ where $A$ is a local
  1352	ring, show that the natural maps are isomorphisms
  1353		$$\Pic_X(A)\risom\Pic_{X/S}(A)\risom\Pic_{(X/S)\zar}(A)$$
  1354	 where $\Pic_X(A):=\Pic_X(T)$, where $\Pic_{X/S}(A):=\Pic_{X/S}(T)$,
  1355	and so forth.
  1356	
  1357	Assume $A$ is Artin local with algebraically closed residue field.  Show
  1358		$$\Pic_X(A)\risom\Pic_{(X/S)\et}(A).$$
  1359	
  1360	Assume $A$ is an algebraically closed  field $k$.  Show
  1361		$$\Pic_X(k)\risom\Pic_{(X/S)\fppf}(k).$$
  1362	  \end{ex}
  1363	
  1364	\begin{ex}\label{ex:Pfs}
  1365	 Show that the natural map
  1366		$$\Pic_{(X/S)\zar}\to \Pic_{(X/S)\et}$$
  1367	 need not be an isomorphism.  Specifically, take $X$ to be the following
  1368	 curve  in the real projective plane:
  1369		$$X:u^2+v^2+w^2=0 \text{ in }\I P^2_\bb R.$$
  1370	 Then $X$ has no $\bb R$-points, but  over the complex numbers $\bb C$,
  1371	 there is an isomorphism
  1372		$$\vf\:X_{\bb C}\risom\I P^1_{\bb C}.$$
  1373	 Show that $\vf^*\mc O(1)$ defines an element of $\Pic_{(X/\bb R)\et}(\bb
  1374	R)$, which is not in the image of $\Pic_{(X/\bb R)\zar}(\bb R)$.
  1375	 \end{ex}
  1376	
  1377	The main result of this section is the following comparison theorem.
  1378	It identifies two useful conditions: the first guarantees that the first
  1379	three relative functors can be viewed as subfunctors of the fourth;
  1380	together, the two conditions guarantee that all four functors coincide.
  1381	The second condition has three successively weaker forms.  Before we can
  1382	prove the theorem, we must develop some theory.
  1383	
  1384	\begin{thm}[Comparison]\label{th:cmp}
  1385	 Assume $\mc O_{\!S}\risom f_*\mc O_{\!X}$ holds universally; that is, for any
  1386	$S$-scheme $T$, the comorphism of $f_T$ is an isomorphism, $\mc O_{\!T}\risom
  1387	f_{\smash{T}*}\mc O_{\!X_T}$.
  1388	 \smallskip
  1389	
  1390	\tu{1.}\enspace
  1391	 Then the natural maps are injections:
  1392		$$\Pic_{X/S}\into \Pic_{(X/S)\zar}\into \Pic_{(X/S)\et}\into
  1393		\Pic_{(X/S)\fppf}.$$
  1394	
  1395	\tu{2.}\enspace All three maps are isomorphisms if also $f$ has a
  1396	section; the latter two maps are isomorphisms if also $f$ has a section
  1397	locally in the Zariski topology; and the last map is isomorphism if also
  1398	$f$ has a section locally in the \'etale topology.
  1399	 \end{thm}
  1400	
  1401	\begin{ex}\label{ex:gpts}
  1402	 Assume $\mc O_{\!S}\risom f_*\mc O_{\!X}$ holds universally.  Using
  1403	Theorem~\ref{th:cmp}, show that its four functors  have the same
  1404	geometric points; in other words, for every algebraically closed field
  1405	$k$ containing the residue class field of a point of $S$, the $k$-points
  1406	of all four functors are, in a natural way, the same.  Show, in fact,
  1407	that these $k$-points are just the elements of $\Pic(X_k)$.
  1408	
  1409	What if $\mc O_{\!S}\risom f_*\mc O_{\!X}$ does not necessarily hold
  1410	universally?

    11	
    12	The admissible coverage parameter is strictly positive, so the chosen representer in

    15	`divRepAffAdmissibleScheme`.

    18	product atlas, and the source is quasi-compact, locally of finite type, and separated over the
